haiku-low.q1: They see the same 200 message: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is written and no email is sent.
haiku-low.q2: The request is refused: the transaction rolls back, nothing is written or sent, and the same 200 confirmation message is shown.
haiku-low.q3: It works 30 minutes from creation (expires_at). It ends sooner if used (used_at set), or when a newer link is issued for the account, which kills earlier unused links.
haiku-low.q4: Nothing is written, so the link stays live (used_at still NULL) and keeps working until expires_at. The user sees the form again with the error.
haiku-low.q5: No devices stay logged in: all sessions for the user are deleted, including the one that did the reset. The user logs in again at /login with the new password.
haiku-low.q6: The worker retries up to 3 times with backoff, then logs the error and drops the job. The user is not told and must request a new reset.
haiku-low.q7: The raw token is generated in API memory and placed in the queued email job's link. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored, and the emailed link carries the raw token.
haiku-low.q8: The API hashes the raw token with SHA-256 and finds the reset_tokens row by token_hash. It accepts only if used_at is NULL and expires_at is later than now.
haiku-low.q9: In the reset_tokens table in Postgres, counting that user's rows with created_at in the last 60 minutes. Old rows are kept, not deleted, and age out of the window.
haiku-low.q10: Inside the issuing transaction, before the new row is inserted, all of the account's unused links get used_at set to now, so they die.
haiku-low.q11: In one transaction: mark the link used, update password_hash, and delete all the user's sessions. The confirmation email is queued only after COMMIT.
haiku-low.q12: The submit uses a conditional UPDATE setting used_at WHERE used_at IS NULL and not expired. The losing submit updates 0 rows, rolls back, and sees the expired-link page.

sonnet.q1: They see the same 200 message: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is written and nothing is sent.
sonnet.q2: The count of the user's reset_tokens rows in the last 60 min is already >= 3, so the transaction rolls back, nothing is written or sent, and the same 200 generic response is returned.
sonnet.q3: A link works 30 minutes (expires_at = created_at + 30 min). It ends sooner if used_at is set: by a newer link being issued for the account (step d), or by a successful reset using it.
sonnet.q4: Still live and unchanged. Nothing is written, used_at stays NULL, and the same link keeps working until its expires_at; the form is shown again with the error.
sonnet.q5: None. All the user's sessions rows are deleted (every device, including the one that did the reset). No session is created; the user is redirected to /login and logs in with the new password.
sonnet.q6: The email worker retries with backoff up to 3 retries, then logs an error and drops the job. The user is not told; they must request again.
sonnet.q7: The raw token is generated in API memory at request time, put into the link in the queued email job (link: https://app/reset?token=<raw>), and the worker sends that job as the email.
sonnet.q8: It looks up reset_tokens by token_hash = SHA-256(raw token from the URL). The link is good only if the row exists AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now. Otherwise the expired-link page is shown.
sonnet.q9: There is no separate counter. It is the count of the account's reset_tokens rows with created_at within the last 60 minutes (live and dead rows both count); old rows age out of the window on their own.
sonnet.q10: Inside the issuing transaction, after the rate-limit check and token generation and before inserting the new row, every earlier unused link for that account is killed by setting used_at = now() (not deleted).
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: mark the reset_tokens row used (used_at = now()), update users.password_hash, and delete all the user's sessions rows. The password-changed email job is enqueued only after COMMIT.
sonnet.q12: The transaction's first step is UPDATE reset_tokens SET used_at = now() WHERE id = row AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now(). Only one submit updates a row; the other gets 0 rows, rolls back, and sees the expired-link page.
